title: Gabber log-smooth modification over a field with fixed base
statement:
Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $X$ be an integral quasi-projective finite-type $F$-scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-kun-projective]; quasi-projective means a locally closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over $F$. Let $B\subset X$ be a closed subset with dense complement $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, whose divisorial log structure $M=\mathcal O_X\cap j_*\mathcal O_U^\times$ is fine saturated and log regular [def-trf-log-regular-pair, def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Assume its triviality locus is exactly $U$, so $(X,B)$ is a log regular pair. Suppose $(X,M)$ is log smooth over the trivial log field $(\operatorname{Spec}F,F^\times)$ [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. Let a finite group $G$ of order invertible in $F$ act on this pair by $F$-automorphisms. Assume the action is generically free, meaning free on geometric points over a dense invariant open. Let $T$ be the complement of the largest such free open.

There exist an integral quasi-projective finite-type $F$-scheme $X'$ and a $G$-equivariant projective birational morphism $h:X'\to X$ [def-kun-projective], where birational means an isomorphism over dense open subschemes, with the following properties. Put $B'=h^{-1}(B\cup T)$ as a closed subset. The divisorial log scheme $(X',B')$ is fine saturated and log regular, and log smooth over the trivial log field, with triviality locus exactly $X'\setminus B'$. The $G$-action on it is very tame: every geometric inertia group has invertible order and acts trivially on the characteristic monoid and on $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O^{\rm sh}_{X',\bar x}/I_{\bar x})$, where $I_{\bar x}$ is generated by nonunit log sections [def-per-very-tame-fs-log-action]. The categorical geometric scheme quotient $p:X'\to P=X'/G$ exists, is finite surjective with orbit geometric fibres and invariant structure sheaf [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. The quotient $P$ is integral and quasi-projective of finite type over $F$, and its invariant direct-image log structure is the divisorial log structure with boundary $p(B')$; this log scheme is fine saturated, log regular, and log smooth over the trivial log field, with triviality locus exactly $P\setminus p(B')$. No perfection assumption on $F$ is imposed; the empty original boundary is allowed.

source.place: Expose X Theorem 1.1, printed pp.135--136, specialized to S=Spec F with the trivial log structure and trivial G-action on S (conditions (i)-(iii)); application to effective component stabilizers in X 2.3 Step 3, pp.151--152. The quotient exists because X' is quasi-projective over F, hence the action is admissible; its quasi-projectivity is the classical quasi-projectivity of finite quotients of quasi-projective schemes. This is a logarithmic modification theorem, with no regular or SNC resolution conclusion.

proof.text: The field $F$ is excellent by [lem-exc-fields-excellent]. Applying [lem-per-quasi-excellent-finite-type-stability] to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ gives quasi-excellence and Noetherianness of $X$; finite type supplies quasi-compactness. Both schemes are separated: projective space is separated by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-separated], a locally closed immersion has diagonal an isomorphism onto its fibre product, and the diagonal of a composite of separated maps is closed (factor it through the pullback of the second diagonal). For the affine field base separatedness over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ follows by the same diagonal argument. The trivial log field is log regular directly: its log ideal and characteristic group are zero and its local ring is a field. The given log map is a map of the log regular pairs $(X,B)\to(\operatorname{Spec}F,\varnothing)$. Every inertia subgroup has order dividing $|G|$, so its order is invertible in every residue field of $X$. Thus the action is tame as required by the absolute construction; generic freeness is assumed.

source.place: X 1.1(i)--(iii), pp.135--136; Stacks 07QW and 07QU for excellence, 01OD for separatedness.

proof.text: Choose the four-stage tower of [lem-per-gabber-absolute-equivariant-modification], with base $\operatorname{Spec}F$, and call its composite $h:X'\to X$. This gives integral fs log regular $X'$, quasi-projective of finite type over $F$, and $h$ equivariant and projective in the finite-projective-space sense. It is an isomorphism over the dense open $X\setminus(B\cup T)$: density follows by intersecting the dense triviality and free opens in integral $X$. Its boundary is exactly $B'=h^{-1}(B\cup T)$, and the final action is very tame in precisely the characteristic-monoid and strict-local-stratum sense in the statement. These are conclusions of the absolute tower, which does not yet assert log smoothness over $F$. We verify that along its specified stages next.

source.place: VIII Theorem 1.1 and 5.6.1; X proof of 1.1, p.139 (use the specified absolute construction).

proof.text: The first two stages of this tower are saturated log blowup towers, making the scheme regular and the boundary strict normal crossings and $G$-strict. They are log etale by [lem-per-log-smooth-composition-strict-base-change]. Composition with the given log smooth morphism to the trivial log field remains log smooth. This starts the induction through the third stage with a regular scheme, a $G$-strict boundary, and log smoothness over the same fixed base.

At each fixed-locus blowup of the finite third-stage procedure, use [lem-per-gabber-fixed-locus-log-chart]. Its hypotheses are the regular strict boundary from the preceding stages, tame action, and the induction hypothesis of log smoothness over the trivially acted-on base. Let $\gamma:Q\to P=\mathbf Z^t\oplus\mathbf N^r$ be the chart map that lemma supplies, with $\gamma^{\rm gp}$ injective and finite cokernel torsion of invertible order. On a $z_i$ blowup chart the new boundary chart is $\mathbf Z^t\oplus\mathbf N^r$ with base map $(1\oplus\beta_i)\gamma$; $\beta_i^{\rm gp}$ is unipotent, hence an automorphism of $\mathbf Z^r$, so kernel and cokernel are those of $\gamma^{\rm gp}$. On a $y_i$ chart it is $\mathbf Z^t\oplus\mathbf N^{r+1}$ with base map $(1\oplus\delta)\gamma$; the images $\delta(e_j)$ together with $e_{r+1}$ form a basis of $\mathbf Z^{r+1}$, so $(1\oplus\delta)^{\rm gp}$ is injective with cokernel $\mathbf Z$ and the new cokernel is $\operatorname{coker}\gamma^{\rm gp}\oplus\mathbf Z$, with the same torsion. (For the trivial log field one may take $Q=0$, where both cokernels are free.) The variables outside that monoid are polynomial variables, hence the scheme comparison to $S\times_{\Lambda[Q]}\Lambda[P']$ is smooth. The chart criterion [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale] proves log smoothness on these covering charts. The chart lemma explicitly identifies the blowup and strict transform with their pullbacks; strict base-change stability and strict etale locality in [lem-per-log-smooth-composition-strict-base-change] therefore give log smoothness for the actual blowup. Iterate this argument through the specified finite permissible procedure of the absolute tower. The third-stage output has abelian inertia, is free outside its boundary, and has the regular strict boundary needed for the fourth stage.

source.place: X 1.4--1.7, pp.141--146, fixed-locus blowup charts; VIII 4.2.13.

proof.text: By [lem-per-projective-finite-group-quotient], applied over the affine Noetherian base $\operatorname{Spec}F$, the quasi-projective scheme $X'$ has a categorical geometric scheme quotient $p:X'\to P$. It is finite surjective with orbit geometric fibres and invariant structure sheaf; $P$ is integral and quasi-projective of finite type over $F$. Inverse images of affine opens of $P$ are invariant affine opens of $X'$ because $p$ is finite; hence the action on $X'$ is admissible. The free dense open of Step 2 is still free under its equivariant isomorphism with the corresponding open of $X$. We may therefore apply [lem-per-very-tame-log-quotient]: $M_P=(p_*M_{X'})^G$ is fs log regular, $p$ is Kummer etale, and the invariant morphism to the trivial log field factors through $P$.

source.place: VI Theorem 3.2 and Proposition 3.5, pp.73--75. Quasi-projectivity and quotient existence: the existing lem-per-projective-finite-group-quotient (Rydh Theorem 4.4, Proposition 4.7, Remark 4.9).

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-gabber-abelian-stage-toric-chart] to the third-stage output $X_3$ of the chosen absolute tower, whose fourth stage is $X'\to X_3$. Step 4 supplies log smoothness over $F$, regularity, the strict $G$-strict boundary, abelian inertia, and freeness off that boundary. Also: $X_3\to X$ is a finite tower of normalized blowups, each projective in the projective-bundle sense, so $X_3$ is integral and of finite type over $X$, hence Noetherian and quasi-excellent by [lem-per-quasi-excellent-finite-type-stability] applied to $X_3\to\operatorname{Spec}F$, and separated by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-separated] and the diagonal argument of Step 1. Let $\gamma:Q\to P$, $\overline P$, $\overline R$, $R$, $\overline R'=\mathbf Z^a\oplus\mathbf N^b$ and $R'=\mathbf Z^a\oplus\mathbf N^c$ be as supplied by the lemma. Then $Q^{\rm gp}\to R'^{\rm gp}$ is injective, since its composite into $\overline R'^{\rm gp}\cong\overline R^{\rm gp}\subset\overline P^{\rm gp}=P^{\rm gp}\oplus\mathbf Z^s$ is $\gamma^{\rm gp}$ followed by an inclusion. Its cokernel embeds in $\overline R'^{\rm gp}/Q^{\rm gp}\cong\overline R^{\rm gp}/Q^{\rm gp}\subset\operatorname{coker}\gamma^{\rm gp}\oplus\mathbf Z^s$, so its torsion is finite of invertible order. The comparison morphism $S\times_{\Lambda[Q]}\Lambda[\overline R']\to S\times_{\Lambda[Q]}\Lambda[R']$ is the base change of affine space of dimension $b-c$ given by the chart lemma, hence smooth. By [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale] these quotient charts are log smooth; the lemma identifies them, after strict base change and strict etale comparison, with charts covering the quotient of the fourth-stage output with precisely the retained boundary. The locality and base-change assertion [lem-per-log-smooth-composition-strict-base-change] therefore give log smoothness of $(P,M_P)$ over the trivial log field. Composition with the log etale map $p$ from Step 5 gives log smoothness of $(X',M_{X'})$ over that same field.

source.place: X 1.8, pp.146--148, retained-boundary monoids and quotient charts; group-completion and torsion check for the lemma's chart Q.

proof.text: It remains to identify the stated quotient boundary, rather than only its invariant log structure. The quotient chart in Step 6 retains exactly the image of the inverse-image original boundary of the fourth stage, so its nontriviality locus is $p(B')$. More explicitly the very-tame quotient lemma gives injective Kummer maps on characteristic monoids: a source characteristic monoid is zero if and only if the target is zero, since every source element has a positive multiple in the image and a sharp fs monoid has torsion-free group completion (if $ng=0$, saturation puts both $g$ and $-g$ in the monoid, so sharpness forces $g=0$). Thus $p^{-1}(P^{\rm triv})=X'\setminus B'$. Orbit fibres and invariance of $B'$ give $P^{\rm triv}=P\setminus p(B')$; $p(B')$ is closed because it is the complement of the open triviality locus, which is open by [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure]. By [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure] applied to the fs log regular quotient from Step 5, $M_P=\mathcal O_P\cap j_*\mathcal O_{P\setminus p(B')}^\times$. The same lemma identifies the log structure on $X'$ with its divisorial structure for the exact boundary $B'$. This proves all boundary and triviality assertions. Every base change above was only for local charts: the global schemes and $h,p$ remain over $F$. No perfectness was used. When $B$ is empty, the construction simply introduces the inverse image of $T$; when $G$ is trivial, the identity modification already satisfies the conclusions.

proof_origin.place: X proof of Theorem 1.1, 1.3--1.8, pp.139--148; VI 3.2--3.5. Fixed trivial field base gives Q=0 in both local chart checks.
